On the left a sofa; in front of it stands a table with a rocking-chair and a couple of other chairs. Above the sofa hangs a mirror; on each side of the mirror portraits of Luther and Melanchthon; underneath these, photographs of members of the family. arxiv-2312-17219.creator: Henrik Johansson, Gregor Kälin, Gustav Mogull, and Bram Verbeek
arxiv-2312-17219.description: Abstract We obtain a color-kinematics-dual representation of the two-loop four-vector amplitude in a general renormalizable massless 𝒩 = 1 \mathcal{N}=1 SYM theory, including internal matter as chiral supermultiplets. arxiv-2508-09840.title: Toward the “platinum standard” of quantum chemistry on quantum computers: perturbative quadruple corrections in unitary coupled cluster theory
arxiv-2508-09840.creator: Zachary W. Windom 1 , Luke Bertels 1 , Daniel Claudino 1 , and Rodney J. Bartlett 2
arxiv-2508-09840.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zachary W. Windom 1 , Luke Bertels 1 , Daniel Claudino 1 , and Rodney J. Bartlett 2. We propose a non-iterative, post hoc correction to the unitary coupled cluster theory with single, double, and triple excitations (UCCSDT) ansatz, which considers the leading-order effects of neglected quadruple excitations. We present two ways to derive this quadruples correction to UCCSDT, henceforth referred to as [Q-6], which leads to an improvement in the correlation energy shown to be correct through sixth-order in many-body perturbation theory (MBPT).

arxiv-2510-25580.title: Micro-packets for real groups of type G 2 \mathrm{G}_{2}
arxiv-2510-25580.creator: Nicolas Arancibia Robert, Leticia Barchini, Paul Mezo
arxiv-2510-25580.description: Abstract In their study of Arthur’s conjectures for real groups, Adams, Barbasch, and Vogan introduced the notion of micro-packets . Micro-packets are finite sets of irreducible representations defined using microlocal geometric methods and characteristic cycles. We explore an action of the Weyl group on characteristic cycles to compute all micro-packets of real groups of type G 2 \mathrm{G}_{2} .
